_comment: This service builds apps/api/Dockerfile: a NODE image. It has no python and
no celery binary, so a Celery start command cannot run here and the container
fails with 'The executable `celery` could not be found'.
That happened: the API service was given `celery ... beat` as a custom start
command while trying to get the scheduler running. Every new deploy then
failed to boot, so Railway kept the previous container alive and retried for
two days showing 'building' -- while the old container went on serving.
Celery belongs to the ENGINE image (apps/engine/Dockerfile), which is Python
and has ffmpeg. The scheduler runs there, on the worker service, via --beat.
A custom start command set in the Railway dashboard OVERRIDES the value below
and the Dockerfile's CMD. If this service will not start, clear that field
first: the image already knows how to run itself.
